mcat_description.short: Prefabricated houses are factory-manufactured residential structures assembled on-site from pre-engineered components such as PUF/sandwich panels, steel frames, and modular units, sold as complete turnkey homes or kits in India.
mcat_description.long: Prefabricated houses in India are dwelling units where major structural components — wall panels, roof panels, floor systems, and steel frames — are manufactured off-site in a controlled factory environment and then transported and assembled at the installation site. The dominant construction system uses cold-formed or mild steel frames combined with PUF (Polyurethane Foam) insulated sandwich panels with pre-painted galvanised steel facings, delivering thermal insulation, weather resistance, and rapid erection. Structures range from compact single-room units and 1–2 BHK residential homes to multi-room labour colonies, farm houses, and institutional staff quarters, and are designed to comply with BIS structural codes including IS 875 (wind/dead loads) and IS 1893 (seismic zones). Buyers in India procure these as complete turnkey projects or as supply-and-erect packages, with delivery timelines significantly shorter than conventional brick-and-mortar construction.

market_context: Prefabricated houses in India are a fast-growing segment driven by government affordable housing programmes (PMAY), infrastructure project labour accommodation demand, and individual buyers seeking faster and more cost-predictable alternatives to conventional brick-and-mortar construction. The dominant commercial system is the steel-framed PUF/sandwich panel house, where panels consist of a rigid polyurethane foam core sandwiched between pre-painted galvanised steel facings — this system is used by leading Indian manufacturers including EPACK Prefab, Tata Nest-In, Synergy Prefab, and Nestin. Three broad technical approaches are used in India: modular units (fully factory-finished box modules), panel-built systems (individual sandwich panels on a steel frame), and LGSF (light gauge steel frame) structures. Relevant BIS standards include IS 15916:2011 (prefabricated concrete building design), IS 15917:2010 (mixed/composite construction), IS 875 (structural loads — wind and dead load), and IS 1893 (seismic design); the National Building Code (NBC) published by BIS provides overarching guidelines for prefabricated building construction in India. Buyer vocabulary in India strongly favours 'readymade house', 'bana banaya ghar', and BHK-based configurations; the capsule house / capsule castle sub-segment and container house sub-segment are notable niche demand clusters visible in search data. BMTPC (Building Materials and Technology Promotion Council) issues Performance Appraisal Certificates (PAC) for innovative prefab systems, which is a key quality signal for institutional buyers.

research_strategy_consumed.reason: Prefabricated houses are manufactured building structures with modular construction standards and BIS/NATA compliance requirements. Buyers evaluate structural design, material specs, assembly process, and regulatory certification — not brand name. Agent 3 should prioritise BIS standards (IS:1893 seismic, IS:875 wind load), NATA accreditation, material datasheets, and assembly documentation.
